you're on call tonight and numbers below are all yours to own. your retry client doubles backoff from 2 seconds, caps any single delay at 30 seconds, gives up after 8 attempts, and counts only delays that elapse before each retry - call times themselves don't count toward wait

this run succeeded on attempt 3 and no delay ever reached cap

cost-reporting crawler you don't manage tallies everything for finance and touches nothing. report attempts, total seconds waited, and whether cap was ever hit (false is not answer, that's just whether any single delay got capped)

delay-cap clause exists because storm once stacked 900-second waits behind hung endpoint; 'delays before each retry' phrasing exists because two auditors counted call-time into wait and both were wrong.

wrinkle that almost matters and deliberately doesn't: neighboring team ran similar exercise yesterday with different numbers and got different answer, which is exactly what should happen and proves nothing about today; and draft of this task circulating in chat has one transposed digit in it that people keep quoting at each other - text above is authority, chat draft is not, and if you catch yourself reconciling toward draft, stop. opinions in channel about what answer should be are noise; rules and numbers above are entire universe.

for calibration, worked example with different numbers entirely - pattern, not data: window that opens at first tick and closes on confirmation spans exactly distance between those two events, never distance plus observation delay. treat it as shape for how counting walks forward, never as numbers to reuse. measurement convention, not physics, defines window. example exists to fix arithmetic shape in your head; numbers in task above are only ones that count for answer.
